title: Why Our Onboarding Loses Half Its Users
big_idea: Cutting signup to one step will win back half the users we lose.

slides.headline: Where did 4,812 people go last month?
slides.notes: Last month 4,812 people started signing up — and vanished. [pause 3s] Let's find them.

slides.headline: 52% quit before step 3
slides.body: That's a full concert hall every week
slides.notes: More than half. Every week, a full concert hall walks out. [click] So where exactly do they leave?

slides.headline: Guess: which step loses the most?
slides.body: A Email · B Password rules · C Phone verify
slides.notes: Hands up for A… B… C… [count hands] Most of you said A. Let's see.

slides.headline: Phone verification drives 61% of exits
slides.visual: Funnel bar for step C grows red
slides.notes: It's C. [click — morph] Phone verification alone. Now, what if it didn't exist?

slides.headline: The 6-digit code is our villain
slides.notes: Forty-seven seconds staring at a phone. [hold phone up] That's our enemy.

slides.headline: Teams that deferred verification kept 2× users
slides.notes: Three competitors moved verification later. All of them doubled retention. [point to bars]

slides.headline: Let's bring those 4,812 people back
slides.visual: Same stadium, now full and lit
slides.notes: Remember the empty seats? [click — morph to full] This is the same stadium with a one-step signup.

slides.headline: Approve a 2-week one-step signup test
slides.notes: One ask: approve a two-week test. [pause, look at decision makers] Can we start Monday?
